searchText: Our devnet-8 direct Builder API is up now if anyone wants to try it: https://devnet8-builder-api.bombora.workers.dev It’s still in the early stages of testing and may have brief downtime while changes are rolled out. Would be great if we could point some validators to it, we’ll be monitoring any failed bids and reveals. (cc <@199561711278227457>) Can anyone tell me why so many payloads are getting orphaned on devnet-8? The vast majority of them are coming from builder 1889, but looking at its configuration it seems to be configured the same way as other buildoor instances, revealing 5000ms into the slot. Agent says it might be a payload publishing issue, but I haven’t confirmed: <@&836981489430036500> > intermittent outbound gossip delay in teku-nethermind-1, after Buildoor submits the payload and before network propagation. seems like late reveal, had my claude look into one case for [135991](https://dora.plataberget.ethpandaops.io/slot/135991) and if you look at [ptc votes](https://dora.plataberget.ethpandaops.io/slot/135992#ptcVotes) then everyone besides nimbus votes that it was untimely, see [report](https://gist.github.com/nflaig/6b78796eba7bfb794b45ff7ddb89a067), so seems plausible that there was a delay between buildoor calling publish api and the payload actually being published, but <@654267572107083777> might be worth to look into why nimbus is voting different than other clients, from lodestar pov, the payload was way too late For that slot it makes sense with those PTC votes. However, for slot 134496 and many others [it doesn't](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/134496#ptcVotes) - 98% voted payload + blob available, yet the payload still got orphaned. https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/134495 payload seems canonical? Sorry, meant [134496](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/134496) but same here https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/134497#ptcVotes, ptc voted against it, next proposer reorged it Ah, I was looking at the wrong slot's PTC votes 🤦‍♂️ then it is likely just the payload being released late indeed can look into it, is it a pattern in general, or specific to this block? general pattern <@586161934425128960> you've been looking at attestations. In the following scenario: - payload is revealed late, PTC votes against it - proposer builds on top of full anyway Attesters need to vote for N+1 anyway. Have you checked this is always the case? I didn't look in devnet but I'm seeing instances in kurtosis where there's votes for (N, empty) in this situation Not sure if clients are voting incorrectly or just not syncing the block in time https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/131403 seems to be such a case, <@498331483732312075> does grandine not reorg late payloads? I'm not that worried about proposers for now though, but yes about attesters https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/131404#attestations seems alright? `teku-geth-1` is interesting, it votes for `(N, full)`, seems strange I think that's fine if they didn't get/process N+1 in time You do have to vote for full even if late yeah that's the only reason I can see two observations so far - nimbus votes timely incorrectly - grandine doesn't reorg late payloads looking at lodestar nodes, we set that block as head ~500ms into the slot Perhaps we should spend some AI tokens trying to put out payloads that are delivered probably late (even better if early but hopefully that's impossible) but that finish executing at 12 seconds. Then analyze proposers/attesters behaviors I'm also interested in payloads that are delivered after 6 seconds but execute fast before 9 seconds and want to publicly shame PTC members that vote present This one should be easy to test <@808969530608451584> just set builddoor to reveal at 6 seconds empty payloads Can be checked in kt should be even better yeah grandine does not reorg late payloads, but they said they will fix it, any update here <@498331483732312075> ? it does check fork choice's `should_build_on_full` in selecting bid https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/blob/9dc532a7031ce33dc70d42763ad028092d50d393/block_producer/src/block_producer.rs#L2293-L2296. I'm checking this issue now https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/131403 was self-built confirmed, it's slower than it should, investigating Our devnet-8 direct Builder API is up found the bug! so the issue is Grandine prepare payload before PTC votes (we still called it after aggregate deadline for post-Gloas block) <@654267572107083777> if you could take a look at Nimbus on why it reorged 138956 that'd be awesome, I think you may have never received that block but I want to know why. It appears missing in Dora https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/138956, it's the only block I missed since I freed space in my disk and I can't explain it yet 955 is prysm Nethremind that was bad, it tried to reorg 954, so in 956 I built on top of 954 correctly, but then Nimbus also reorgs my block and builds on top of 954 as well I think no one saw my block, but it you did see it and was invalid that'd be nice to know, Claude tells me that it doesn't have logs expressive enough from Nimbus getting logs

excerpts.author: serenita_io
excerpts.content:
Can anyone tell me why so many payloads are getting orphaned on devnet-8?
The vast majority of them are coming from builder 1889, but looking at its configuration it seems to be configured the same way as other buildoor instances, revealing 5000ms into the slot.

excerpts.author: jimmygchen
excerpts.content:
Agent says it might be a payload publishing issue, but I haven’t confirmed: <@&836981489430036500> 

> intermittent outbound gossip delay in teku-nethermind-1, after Buildoor submits the payload and before network propagation.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: seems like late reveal, had my claude look into one case for [135991](https://dora.plataberget.ethpandaops.io/slot/135991) and if you look at [ptc votes](https://dora.plataberget.ethpandaops.io/slot/135992#ptcVotes) then everyone besides nimbus votes that it was untimely, see [report](https://gist.github.com/nflaig/6b78796eba7bfb794b45ff7ddb89a067), so seems plausible that there was a delay between buildoor calling publish api and the payload actually being published, but <@654267572107083777> might be worth to look into why nimbus is voting different than other clients, from lodestar pov, the payload was way too late

excerpts.author: serenita_io
excerpts.content: For that slot it makes sense with those PTC votes. However, for slot 134496 and many others [it doesn't](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/134496#ptcVotes) - 98% voted payload + blob available, yet the payload still got orphaned.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
<@586161934425128960> you've been looking at attestations. In the following scenario: 
- payload is revealed late, PTC votes against it
- proposer builds on top of full anyway

Attesters need to vote for N+1 anyway. Have you checked this is always the case? 

I didn't look in devnet but I'm seeing instances in kurtosis where there's votes for (N, empty) in this situation

excerpts.content: Not sure if clients are voting incorrectly or just not syncing the block in time
